summary:
SPACE WARS is an interactive, NASA-inspired space adventure game designed for children aged 7–12. It transforms space science and astronaut training into a fun, colorful, and educational gaming experience. Players take on the role of junior astronauts and complete missions involving rocket launches, space exploration, planetary landings, space station survival, radiation safety, and communication.

The project integrates real NASA data, including information from NASA's DONKI service, to introduce players to actual space weather events such as coronal mass ejections, solar flares, and radiation-related alerts. These events help create science-based mission scenarios, allowing children to understand how real space conditions can affect astronauts and spacecraft.

By combining interactive gameplay, simple instructions, mission-based challenges, and real-world space science, SPACE WARS makes complex space concepts easier for young learners to understand. Our goal is to inspire curiosity about astronomy, science, and space exploration while helping children learn through playing.
details:
SPACE WARS

SPACE WARS is a browser-based educational space adventure game designed for children aged 7–12. It transforms astronaut training and space exploration into interactive missions where players learn by doing rather than simply reading information or answering repetitive quizzes.

How It Works

Players become junior astronauts and progress through space missions involving rocket launches, spacecraft navigation, planetary exploration, safe landings, space station construction, oxygen management, radiation protection, and communication with Earth. Each mission contains objectives, challenges, clues, and simple instructions. Players must complete the required tasks to unlock the next stage. If they fail, they can retry and improve their performance.

NASA Data Integration

The project connects with NASA data services, particularly NASA's DONKI (Space Weather Database Of Notifications, Knowledge, Information). Real space-weather information, including coronal mass ejections, solar flares, and radiation-related events, can be used to create science-based mission conditions. This helps children understand how actual space events can affect spacecraft and astronauts. Other NASA resources, such as OSDR, RadLab, and Mars Trek, support the project's broader educational direction. Real NASA information is distinguished from simulated gameplay scenarios.

Technologies Used

  • Frontend: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript
  • Backend: Node.js and JavaScript
  • API Integration: NASA Open APIs and DONKI
  • Deployment: Vercel
  • Development Tools: Visual Studio Code, Git, and GitHub
  • Data Handling: Server-side API routes to securely communicate with NASA services

Benefits and Intended Impact

SPACE WARS makes space science more accessible and enjoyable for young learners. It encourages problem-solving, logical thinking, curiosity, decision-making, and basic scientific understanding. Children learn about real space phenomena through interactive experiences instead of complex scientific explanations.

Creativity and Design Considerations

The game combines colorful visuals, animations, mission progression, interactive controls, simple language, and retry options to create a child-friendly experience. We considered the target age group, ease of navigation, learning objectives, gameplay difficulty, accessibility, and the accuracy of NASA-related information.

Our ultimate goal is to inspire the next generation of space explorers by making science education interactive, engaging, and connected to real-world space research.
